g.text: Lab 5.3 — Network monitoring
Three tools that answer three different questions — pick by the question, not by the symptom
1 · Network Watcher — one tool per question
"is an NSG rule dropping this packet?"
IP Flow Verify — you give it source, destination, port and direction,
it names the exact rule that allowed or denied the packet
"where does this traffic actually go?"
Next Hop — returns the hop type and the route that produced it,
which is how you catch a user-defined route you forgot about
"can A reach B right now, end to end?"
Connection Troubleshoot — sends real traffic and reports every hop,
so it sees the things a rule check cannot: a dead service, a full disk
The first two evaluate configuration. Only the third proves that traffic actually flows.
2 · Flow logs are a separate pipeline
prod-...-swc-vnet
VNet flow log
platformskycraftswcsa
platform-...-swc-law
traffic enabled per VNet raw logs land here Traffic Analytics rolls
formatVersion 2 retention 7 days them up every 10 min
Flow logs need a storage account first — that is why this lab depends on Lab 4.1.
az CLI — the check this lab actually runs
az network watcher test-ip-flow \
--vm dev-skycraft-swc-auth-vm -g dev-skycraft-swc-rg \
--direction Inbound --protocol TCP \
# answer: Deny, and the name of the rule that did it — usually DenyAllInBound
